title: Stock
one: Stock that is always right: sell, receive and reorder, with a count that can never go below zero.
marks: This chapter is where the examiner looks for data that stays right under every action: a count that can never go below zero, and a bike that can never be sold twice.

screens.title: See what you will build in this chapter.

blocks.p: The shop keeps two kinds of stock. Parts are counted: there are five 9-speed chains on the shelf, and the number goes down when one is sold and up when a box arrives. Bikes are one thing each: a bike has a frame number, and it is available, reserved, sold or in repair. Nobody counts bikes, because each one is its own row. This chapter builds the screens for both, and the stored procedures underneath them that keep every count and every status right.

blocks.p: By the end, the counter staff can sell a part, refund it, order more and receive the delivery. They can reserve a bike, sell it once and only once, and send it for repair. They can hand a hire bike over, take it back and cancel a hire that never started. Every one of those is one stored procedure, and every stored procedure refuses when the action makes no sense.

words: Stock
The things the shop has to sell or to hire out right now.
Count
The number of one part on the shelf, which the Part table keeps in its QtyInStock column.
Guard
A check inside a stored procedure that refuses an action before any row is changed.
Reorder level
The count at which the shop should order more of a part.
Reorder quantity
How many of a part the shop usually orders at a time.
Walk-in customer
A customer who buys at the counter without an account, saved as no customer at all.
Refund
Taking a sale back, so the parts return to the shelf and the sale row is marked Refunded.
Delivery
A box from a supplier arriving, which closes an order and adds its contents to the count.
Status
One word that says where a thing is in its life, such as Available, Reserved or Sold.
Reserve
Holding a bike for sale for one customer, so nobody else can buy it.

screens.title: Read how a count stays right.

blocks.p: Every change to the count of a part goes through one of three stored procedures: a sale takes some off, a refund puts them back, and a delivery adds a box. No screen ever types a new count into the Part table. That is the whole idea. If the only way in is through those three doors, and each door checks before it opens, the count is always right.
The table below plays out one part through a day. Press the button to switch the guard off and watch what happens to the count.

ledger.offLine: Without the guard, the database would have let the shop sell what it does not have, and the count would be a lie from then on.

rows.what: The day starts with five chains on the shelf
Another customer asks for three more
A box of ten arrives from the supplier
The first customer brings their three back for a refund

rule.text: The count of a part is only ever changed by a sale, a refund or a delivery, and a sale is refused before the count can go below zero. The check is inside the stored procedure, so every screen gets it for free.

screens.title: Read how a bike is one thing, not a count.

blocks.p: A bike is never counted, because every bike is different: its own frame number, size and colour. Instead, each bike has a status. A bike for sale starts as Available. A customer can reserve it, which makes it Reserved and remembers who. Then it is sold, once, and becomes Sold with the date. Any bike can go into repair and come back.

box.title: The life of a bike for sale
box.text: Available, then Reserved for one customer, then Sold to that customer. Reserved can go back to Available if the customer changes their mind. Sold is the end: a sold bike is never sold again, and the stored procedure in stage 6 makes sure of it.

box.title: The life of a hire bike
box.text: A hire bike stays Available and goes out and comes back through its hires. Each hire has its own status: Booked, then Out, then Returned, or Cancelled if it never started. The free list in stage 6 offers only the hire bikes with no Booked or Out hire on those dates, which is the clash test from chapter 7 with dates instead of times.

blocks.p: Each step in those lives is one stored procedure, and each one checks that the bike is in the right status first. A sold bike cannot be reserved. A bike that is not in repair cannot come back from repair. The checks are the same shape every time: IF NOT EXISTS a row in the right status, refuse.

code.title: usp_PartSale_GetByDateRange: the sales between two dates, with names
parts: The name, and what goes in and out
Two dates go in. A table of rows comes back, so there is no @Message.
Each row is one sale: its number and time, the part code and name, the customer or the word Walk-in, how many at what price, the total worked out on the spot, who sold it, and its status.

Four tables joined. LEFT JOIN Customer keeps the walk-in sales, which have no customer row. CAST(ps.SoldOn AS DATE) throws away the clock part so that BETWEEN works on whole days. Newest first. GO ends the batch, ready for the next stored procedure.
code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_PartSale_GetByDateRange
    @FromDate DATE,
    @ToDate   DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT ps.PartSaleID, ps.SoldOn, p.PartCode, p.Name AS Part,
           ISNULL(c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName, 'Walk-in') AS Customer,
           ps.Quantity, ps.UnitPrice,
           ps.Quantity * ps.UnitPrice AS Total,
           st.FirstName + ' ' + st.LastName AS SoldBy,
           ps.Status
    FROM PartSale ps
    JOIN Part      p  ON p.PartID      = ps.PartID
    LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerID = ps.CustomerID
    JOIN Staff     st ON st.StaffID    = ps.SoldByStaffID
    WHERE CAST(ps.SoldOn AS DATE) BETWEEN @FromDate AND @ToDate
    ORDER BY ps.SoldOn DESC;
END
GO

blocks.p: When the box arrives, two things must both happen: the order closes, and the count goes up by what was in the box. If only one of them happened, the shop would either count the same box twice or never count it at all. Putting both UPDATEs inside one stored procedure is how the two stay together. You type those two UPDATEs.

code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_PartOrder_GetOpen
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT o.PartOrderID, p.PartCode, p.Name AS Part, s.Name AS Supplier,
           o.QtyOrdered, o.OrderedOn, o.ExpectedOn,
           st.FirstName + ' ' + st.LastName AS PlacedBy
    FROM PartOrder o
    JOIN Part     p  ON p.PartID      = o.PartID
    JOIN Supplier s  ON s.SupplierID  = p.SupplierID
    JOIN Staff    st ON st.StaffID    = o.PlacedByStaffID
    WHERE o.Status = 'Ordered'
    ORDER BY o.ExpectedOn, p.Name;
END

code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_Part_GetReorderList
AS
BEGIN
    -- Parts at or below their reorder level that have no order on the way.
    SELECT p.PartID, p.PartCode, p.Name, s.Name AS Supplier, s.Phone
        AS SupplierPhone,
           p.QtyInStock, p.ReorderLevel, p.ReorderQty
    FROM Part p
    JOIN Supplier s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
    WHERE p.QtyInStock <= p.ReorderLevel
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM PartOrder o WHERE o.PartID = p.PartID
          AND o.Status = 'Ordered')
    ORDER BY s.Name, p.Name;
END
GO

code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_Bike_GetAll
    @Purpose VARCHAR(4)      -- 'Hire', 'Sale' or NULL for every bike
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT b.BikeID, b.FrameNumber,
           b.Make + ' ' + b.Model AS Bike,
           b.Size, b.Colour, b.Purpose, b.DailyRate, b.SalePrice, b.Status,
           c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS Customer,
           b.SoldOn
    FROM Bike b
    LEFT JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerID = b.CustomerID
    WHERE @Purpose IS NULL OR b.Purpose = @Purpose
    ORDER BY b.Purpose, b.Make, b.Model, b.Size;
END
GO

parts: The name, and what goes in and out
The start date and the return date. A table comes back.
The bike number, one Display column that joins the make, model, size, colour and frame number into a sentence for the list, and the daily rate for the cost line.
Only hire bikes that are available
A bike for sale is never offered, and neither is a bike in repair.
And no hire of it overlaps the dates
The clash test. A hire of this bike, Booked or Out, that starts before the new return date and ends after the new start date, overlaps. If there is one, the bike is left out.

code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_Bike_GetAvailableForHire
    @StartDate DATE,
    @EndDate   DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT b.BikeID,
           b.Make + ' ' + b.Model + ' · ' + b.Size + ' · ' + b.Colour + ' ('
               + b.FrameNumber + ')' AS Display,
           b.DailyRate
    FROM Bike b
    WHERE b.Purpose = 'Hire'
      AND b.Status  = 'Available'
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT *
                      FROM Hire h
                      WHERE h.BikeID = b.BikeID
                        AND h.Status IN ('Booked', 'Out')
                        AND @StartDate < h.EndDate
                        AND @EndDate   > h.StartDate)
    ORDER BY b.Make, b.Model, b.Size;
END
GO

code.text:
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_Hire_GetByDateRange
    @FromDate DATE,
    @ToDate   DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT h.HireID,
           b.Make + ' ' + b.Model + ' (' + b.Size + ')' AS Bike,
           c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS Customer,
           h.StartDate, h.EndDate,
           DATEDIFF(DAY, h.StartDate, h.EndDate) AS Days,
           h.TotalCost, h.DepositPaid, h.Status
    FROM Hire h
    JOIN Bike     b ON b.BikeID     = h.BikeID
    JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
    WHERE h.StartDate <= @ToDate AND h.EndDate >= @FromDate
    ORDER BY h.StartDate, b.Make;
END
GO

CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE usp_Hire_GetForBike
    @BikeID INT
AS
BEGIN

    WHERE h.BikeID = @BikeID

The Giant Escape 3 S is not among them, because hire 3 has it out until the day after tomorrow, and neither is the Frog 62, because it is in repair. The cost line reads 1 day × £16.00 = £16.00 · deposit at least £3.20 for the first bike in the list, and the deposit box holds that amount.

img.alt: The new hire form running: Hannah Boyle picked, the start day Monday 12 October and the return day Tuesday 13 October, and the bike list dropped down showing four bikes: Giant Escape 3 M Grey, Specialized Sirrus 2.0 L Black, Trek FX 2 L Blue and Trek FX 2 M Blue, each with its frame number.
img.cap: The new hire form with the bike list open. Only the bikes free for all of those days are offered. When the list closes, the cost and the smallest deposit show under it.

marks.say: Four bikes are offered. The Giant Escape 3 S is missing because hire 3 has it out until the day after tomorrow, and the Frog 62 is missing because it is in repair.

steps.do: Pick the Trek FX 2 M, change the deposit to 1, and press Book hire.
steps.see: A message box says: The deposit must be at least £3.60 (20% of £18.00). The stored procedure from chapter 7 worked that out, and the form only passed the sentence on.

steps.do: Press OK. The form fills the bike list again, in case another booking took a bike while you typed, so the list is back on its first bike. Pick the Trek FX 2 M again: the deposit box changes to 3.60 by itself. Press Book hire.
steps.see: The form closes, and your hire is in the grid as Booked.

steps.do: Pick your new hire and press Check out. Answer Yes.
steps.see: Booked becomes Out, and only Return is on for it.

steps.do: Press Return. Answer Yes.
steps.see: Out becomes Returned, and all three buttons are off.

wrong.q: Nothing happens when you press Bike hire
wrong.a: The Click event is not wired. In the designer, click the button, open the Properties window, press the lightning bolt and check that Click has a method beside it.

wrong.q: The bike list is empty for tomorrow
wrong.a: An empty list means every hire bike is already booked, out or in repair for those dates. Check the dates, then check your usp_Bike_GetAvailableForHire against the block in stage 6.
The return date is the same as the start date. The date pickers push it on when they are wired: double-click dtpStart in the designer and check that its ValueChanged method is there.

stages.title: The reorder list in the program

screens.title: Walk a part from low stock to a full shelf.

blocks.p: This screen plays out stage 1 in the running program. A part runs low, the shop orders more, the box arrives, and the count is right at every step without anyone typing a number into the Part table.

steps.do: Press Parts and stock on the main menu, and press Reorder list.
steps.see: The top grid shows only PADS-DISC and TYRE-700-35, with a Supplier phone column, and the button now reads Show all parts. CHAIN-11 is not there, because order 3 for it is open.

img.alt: The parts screen after pressing Reorder list: the top grid shows only PADS-DISC and TYRE-700-35, with a Supplier phone column, and the button now reads Show all parts.
img.cap: The reorder list in the program: the same two rows as the test in stage 4, with the supplier phone number ready to ring.

marks.say: Only the parts to order. CHAIN-11 is gone because its order is open.
The button has swapped its words. Press it again to see every part.

steps.do: Pick TYRE-700-35 and press Place order.
steps.see: The order form opens, with the quantity at the usual reorder amount for the tyre and the expected date a week away.

steps.do: Press Place order on the order form, without changing the quantity or the date.
steps.see: The form closes. The order is in the lower grid, and TYRE-700-35 has left the reorder list, because an order for it is now open. The count has not changed.

steps.do: Press Show all parts, then pick order 3 for CHAIN-11 in the lower grid and press Receive delivery.
steps.see: The receive form opens, with the order summary and 6 ordered at the top, and 6 in the received box.

img.alt: The receive form running over the parts screen, reading CHAIN-11 · Chain, 11-speed from Northern Components Ltd, 6 ordered, with 6 in the Received box.
img.cap: Receiving order 3. One press closes the order and adds six to the count of CHAIN-11.

marks.say: The summary and the ordered amount came from the row you picked.
Change the number only if the box was short.

steps.do: Leave the number at 6 and press Receive.
steps.see: The order leaves the lower grid, and CHAIN-11 in the top grid goes from 1 to 7 and loses its pink tint, in one press.

steps.do: Pick your tyre order in the lower grid and press Cancel order. Answer Yes.
steps.see: The order leaves the lower grid. Press Reorder list: TYRE-700-35 is back on it, because its count is still low and no order is open.

rule.text: Every count you saw change was changed by a stored procedure, and the screen only asked for the rows again. If the examiner types a sale for more than you have, the answer is a sentence, never a minus number.

screens.title: Run every test in your program.

blocks.p: Every row below is a test the examiner would run. The ones marked Must be refused are the important ones. If one of those gets through, the count is wrong or a bike is sold twice, however nice the screens look. Do each one in your running program where it says, or in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) where no screen can reach it, and tick it when you have seen the result. Part 4 is PADS-DISC with 2 in stock in the sample data: run your whole script first if its count has changed.

check.what: Sell a part with enough stock
check.how: Parts and stock, pick CHAIN-9, Sell, quantity 1. The row's count goes down by one.

check.what: Sell more than is in stock
check.how: Pick PADS-DISC with 2 in stock, Sell, quantity 3. Message: Only 2 in stock.

check.what: The count is untouched after a refusal
check.how: After the refusal, PADS-DISC still shows 2. Nothing was taken off.

check.what: Sell exactly what is in stock
check.how: PADS-DISC, Sell, quantity 2. The row shows 0, and it is pink.

check.what: A refund puts the stock back
check.how: In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), run the refund test from stage 3 with the number of that sale. The count printed is 2 again.

check.what: Refund the same sale twice
check.how: Press F5 again in the refund test. Message: That sale has already been refunded, or does not exist.

check.what: A delivery closes the order and adds to the count
check.how: Parts and stock, pick an open order, Receive. The order leaves the lower grid and the part's count goes up by the number received.

check.what: Receive the same order twice
check.how: The order is gone from the grid, so no button can reach it. In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), run the receive test from stage 4 with its number. Message: That order is not open.

check.what: Cancel an order twice
check.how: In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), run the cancel test from stage 4. The second cancel is refused: Only an open order can be cancelled.

check.what: A part on the reorder list has no open order
check.how: Order more of a part on the reorder list. It leaves the list until the order is received or cancelled.

check.what: Sell a bike that is sold
check.how: Bikes, pick a Sold bike: the Sell button is off. In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), run the bike sale test from stage 6: Bike 11 is refused with That bike has already been sold.

check.what: Sell a reserved bike to another customer
check.how: Reserve an available bike for one customer, pick another customer in the list, Sell, Yes. Message: That bike is reserved for another customer.

check.what: Sell a reserved bike to the customer who reserved it
check.how: Pick the reserving customer, Sell, Yes. The bike is Sold with today's date.

check.what: A bike in repair cannot be reserved or sold
check.how: Pick a bike that is In repair. Reserve and Sell are off, and the repair button reads Back in service.

check.what: A hire whose dates overlap another hire
check.how: Bike hire, New hire, dates inside an existing Booked hire. That bike is not in the list. In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), the hire test from chapter 7 with those dates is refused: That bike is already out on those dates.

check.what: A hire starting the day another ends
check.how: New hire, start date the day an existing hire ends. The bike is in the list, and the booking is made.

check.what: Too small a deposit
check.how: New hire, deposit 1, Book. Message: The deposit must be at least the amount the cost line shows.

check.what: A bike for sale cannot be hired
check.how: New hire: no bike for sale is ever in the list. In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), the hire test from chapter 7 with @BikeID = 7 is refused: Choose a hire bike.

check.what: Check out, then return
check.how: Pick a Booked hire, Check out, Yes: it is Out. Return, Yes: it is Returned.

check.what: Return a hire that is not out
check.how: Pick a Returned hire: Return is off. In SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), run the return test from stage 8 with its number. Message: Only a hire that is out can be returned.

screens.title: Finish the chapter.

blocks.p: Twenty ticks are your evidence that the counts and the statuses hold. Keep the screenshots for your testing evidence in chapter 10. When you want the sample data back, click in BikeShop.sql and press F5 with nothing selected: every count and every status returns to where this chapter started.

box.title: Make it yours
box.text: Your scenario will have its own counted things and its own one-of-a-kind things. Write down which is which: what gets counted, such as tickets, seats or boxes of stock, and what has a status of its own, such as a room, a van or a loan. For each counted thing, name the three stored procedures that are the only doors to its count. For each thing with a status, draw its life as a line of status words, and write one IF NOT EXISTS check for each step along it.
